In case of a manual update of the dependencies list, please ensure the list stays alphabetically sorted.
How to update dependencies
satis and composer.tiki.org
First, make sure the version you want is covered by
doc/devtools/satis.json,  as that's what makes the
package available on composer.tiki.org
NOTE: composer.tiki.org is only used up to Tiki 28.x.
For Tiki 29.x and above, dependencies use public repositories like Packagist.org.
check composer.json:
composer -d vendor_bundled update --dry-run
update composer.lock:
composer -d vendor_bundled update
Useful to look at:
composer -d vendor_bundled outdated
This is what setup.sh runs:
composer -d vendor_bundled install --prefer-dist #In dev mode
composer -d vendor_bundled install --prefer-dist --no-dev #In release mode
NOTE ON VERSION CONSTRAINTS:
As of 2025-04, we use the tilde (~) operator instead of caret (^) for all dependencies.
This file is automatically checked in CI by .gitlab-ci.yml using doc/devtools/check_caret_operator.sh to ensure the use of ~ instead of ^ in version constraints.
This change aims to prevent unexpected upgrades caused by packages that do not strictly follow semantic versioning.
The caret (^) operator (e.g., ^1.10.0) allows updates up to the next major version (<2.0.0).
This can introduce breaking changes if the package does not adhere strictly to SemVer.
The tilde (~) operator offers tighter control:
- ~3.0 allows updates up to <3.1.0 (safe minor & patch updates)
- ~3.0.0 allows only patch updates (<3.0.1)
Recommendation: use version constraints like ~3.0 rather than ~3.0.0,
Using ~3.0 ensures we continue to receive non-breaking feature improvements without being locked into a specific minor release for an extended period.
Major version bumps (e.g., from 3.x to 4.x) must be handled explicitly in a dedicated commit.
This ensures that we are aware of potential breaking changes and can test accordingly.
Do not use exact versions (e.g., '1.10.57'), wildcards (e.g., '*'), or dev (e.g., 'dev-master') branches unless necessary.
See: https://getcomposer.org/doc/articles/versions.md#tilde-version-range-
Please follow this convention when adding or updating entries in composer.json dependencies.

Packages with non-standard version constraints that require explanation.
This includes both unstable versions (dev-master, etc.) and stable versions that aren't the latest available.
TOOL USAGE:
This list is used by the Composer Stability Checker script (doc/devtools/check_composer_stability.php).
The script analyzes package stability across Tiki versions and flags non-standard constraints.
When packages are listed here, they are marked as [MITIGATED] in the script output.
BRANCH PRESENCE:
The stability checker script may only be present in newer versions (master/29.x+) because:
1. The script is part of the release process and development tooling
2. Since the script compares across all available Tiki versions, being only on master can be sufficient
3. The ignore list itself provides documentation for dependency decisions across all versions
4. Older branches don't need the script since they're analyzed from the master version
SPLIT DOCUMENTATION:
Package documentation is now split between two locations in this composer.json file:
1. This stability-ignore list (under 'extra'): Documents why specific version constraints are acceptable
2. The main _comment section above: Explains package purpose, usage, and general dependency notes
This separation allows for:
- Clear distinction between 'what' (package docs in _comment) and 'why' (stability justification here)
- Focused stability analysis without cluttering general documentation
- Easier maintenance of stability justifications vs. feature documentation
- Better organization: stability concerns are isolated from general package information
NOTE:
This stability-ignore list will be included in all supported Tiki versions because:
1. It provides valuable context for dependency decisions across all supported versions
2. Helps maintain consistency in dependency management practices
3. Enables the stability checker tool to work properly when analyzing from master
4. Documents decisions that may affect future dependency updates
5. Ensures all versions have the same understanding of acceptable version constraints
Each entry should include:
- reason: Why this specific version constraint is necessary/acceptable
- mitigation: How risk is reduced or managed
- reviewed: Date when decision was reviewed
- reviewer: Name of person who reviewed this decision
- alternatives: What alternatives were considered (if any)
- impact: What functionality would be lost without this package

candy-chat/xmpp-prebind-php.reason: Essential XMPP prebinding for chat system authentication and session management.
candy-chat/xmpp-prebind-php.mitigation: PHP 8 compatibility via patches. Extended with custom TIKITOKEN auth.
candy-chat/xmpp-prebind-php.alternatives: No alternatives for prebinding. Custom implementation would be complex.
candy-chat/xmpp-prebind-php.impact: XMPP chat completely non-functional. Users cannot authenticate or connect.

jason-munro/cypht.reason: Intentionally using dev-master to align with Cypht's master branch during active development of Tiki.
jason-munro/cypht.mitigation: Deep integration with custom patches. Reviewed regularly. When Tiki branches to a stable version, it should switch to the latest stable Cypht release.
jason-munro/cypht.alternatives: Use latest stable in stable branches.
jason-munro/cypht.impact: Webmail completely non-functional. Users lose email access.

garethp/php-ews.reason: Required by Cypht. Currently using dev-master due to needed features not yet available in stable.
garethp/php-ews.mitigation: Monitored for upstream changes. Plan to migrate to stable once required features are released.
garethp/php-ews.alternatives: Recommendation: Consider migrating to stable v0.11.0 unless dev-master features are needed
garethp/php-ews.impact: Exchange integration may be affected if removed.

symfony/polyfill-ctype.reason: Provides ctype_* functions when ext-ctype extension is not available.
symfony/polyfill-ctype.mitigation: Version ~1.8 required by Symfony 6.4 components. Provides fallback functionality.
symfony/polyfill-ctype.alternatives: No alternatives for ctype function polyfills.
symfony/polyfill-ctype.impact: Symfony components fail. System likely unusable due to cascading failures.

config._comment: platform-check CANNOT be enabled, because it would check the ext-* requirements of our dependencies not just ours.  See the workarounds below.  So anything that uses the autoloader, including console.php wouldn't work on a server without ext-soap installed.  Note that platform-check will NOT check the maximum php version anyway, even if we put it in our requires.  In platform, php: The oldest version we support, so composer doesn't pick packages that are incompatible with it (nothing to do with what is checked if we enable platform-check).  On the other hand: ext-*: 0 are workarounds.  ext-ldap is in the require of laminas/laminas-ldap. ext-soap is in the require of laminas/laminas-soap.  We couldn't composer install without this workaround if php-ldap or php-soap aren't installed
